Problem Statement: To analyze the features, benefits, and drawbacks of various DBMSs developed over time to address evolving challenges
Key Findings: Presents advantages and disadvantages of different systems from 1960-2022, helping researchers explore related issues

Problem Statement: Examines foundational role and operational requirements of DBMS in contemporary applications
Key Findings: Relational databases guarantee consistency for structured data; non-relational offer flexibility for unstructured data

Problem Statement: Identifies Big Data as defining challenge with enormous opportunities for database research
Key Findings: Outlines five key research areas required to address Big Data challenge

Problem Statement: Traditional RDBMS face challenges storing/querying dynamic user data for large-scale, high-concurrency applications
Key Findings: Classifies NoSQL databases according to CAP theorem; extracts properties to help enterprise selection

Problem Statement: Addresses design trade-offs in networked shared-data systems as defined by CAP theorem
Key Findings: Designers can achieve trade-off of all three CAP properties by managing partitions effectively

Problem Statement: Analyzes limitations of traditional data management approaches in scalability and flexibility for modern needs
Key Findings: Highlights selection criteria (data model, scalability, consistency) and future directions like AI-driven management

Problem Statement: DBMS performance comparisons often don't reflect real-world use and lack sufficient detail for replication
Key Findings: Performance tests are typically not representative of real scenarios and lack sufficient reporting detail

Problem Statement: Efficient algorithms needed to manipulate large sets and complex objects with performance comparable to simple record processing
Key Findings: Provides foundational understanding of algorithm and architectural issues for designing query execution facilities

Problem Statement: To provide framework for understanding query processing and optimization in RDBMS
Key Findings: Offers basic framework for understanding the field of query processing and optimization

Problem Statement: Provides high-level synthesis of extensive field of query optimization for SQL in relational databases
Key Findings: Explains core foundations of relational query optimization, providing accessible entry point

Problem Statement: Magic sets rewriting produces many variant plans with greatly differing performance; needs method to select best
Key Findings: Cost-based technique performs well, preventing poor decisions that occur without variant selection

Problem Statement: Poorly optimized queries cause slow response times and high resource consumption affecting system performance
Key Findings: Demonstrates practical application of optimization strategies across SQL, NoSQL, and NewSQL databases

Problem Statement: Optimizing queries in distributed relational databases challenged by data distribution, network latency, and varying resources
Key Findings: Identifies gaps and future directions, highlighting trends like ML-assisted optimization

Problem Statement: Traditional RDBMS challenged by volume, velocity, and variety of Big Data
Key Findings: Evaluates performance, scalability, and suitability of various NoSQL databases for Big Data scenarios

Problem Statement: Optimizing query execution in distributed NoSQL databases handling unstructured/semi-structured data
Key Findings: Demonstrates application in large-scale systems and indicates trends with ML, serverless integration

Problem Statement: Organizations face optimization challenges transitioning databases to cloud to control costs and ensure performance
Key Findings: Collective implementation yields improvements in responsiveness while reducing operational expenditures

Problem Statement: Explore application of DL for efficient query processing in IoT databases handling large-scale, time-sensitive data
Key Findings: Optimized model shows higher training efficiency, better energy consumption, and lower latency at scale

Problem Statement: Traditional optimization techniques struggle with complexity and dynamic nature of modern, large-scale databases
Key Findings: AI-driven optimization offers transformative potential for responsive, cost-effective data management

Problem Statement: Traditional query optimization methods are inflexible for highly dynamic or complex workloads
Key Findings: AI-driven models (CatBoost: 59% accuracy) outperform traditional methods (48%), with interpretability trade-offs

Problem Statement: Existing cost models for Spark SQL are rule-based; learning-based models ignore resource allocation
Key Findings: Model outperforms traditional rule-based methods and other learning-based optimizers

Problem Statement: State-of-the-art models fail to quantify query interaction essential for predicting response time in concurrent workloads
Key Findings: Models achieve low prediction error (12% static, 35% dynamic); scheduler outperforms conventional by 2.9x

Problem Statement: ORM frameworks introduce database-related performance inefficiencies in web applications
Key Findings: Fixing identified inefficiencies can reduce query time (up to 91%) and webpage response time (up to 98%)
